question: A 36-year-old woman comes to the physician to discuss contraceptive options. She is currently sexually active with one male partner, and they have not been using any contraception. She has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 15 years. She is allergic to latex and copper. A urine pregnancy test is negative. Which of the following contraceptive methods is contraindicated in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "36-year-old woman" -> "smokes one pack of cigarettes daily" -> "increased risk of thromboembolic events" -> "combined oral contraceptive pill contraindicated" -> 85%

CHAIN: "36-year-old woman" -> "negative urine pregnancy test" -> "not currently pregnant" -> "consider contraceptive options" -> "smoking history affects choice" -> "combined oral contraceptive pill contraindicated" -> 90%

CHAIN: "36-year-old woman" -> "allergic to latex and copper" -> "cannot use diaphragm or IUD" -> "consider other contraceptive methods" -> "smoking history raises risk" -> "combined oral contraceptive pill contraindicated" -> 80%
CHAIN: "36-year-old woman" -> "smokes one pack of cigarettes daily" -> "increased cardiovascular risk" -> "combined oral contraceptive pill not recommended" -> 90%
analysis: The patient is a 36-year-old woman who has a significant smoking history (one pack daily for 15 years). This places her at increased risk for cardiovascular complications if she were to use combined hormonal contraceptives. Therefore, the combined oral contraceptive pill is contraindicated in this patient due to her smoking status and age, as per guidelines that recommend against the use of combined hormonal contraceptives in women over 35 who smoke more than 15 cigarettes per day.
